requirements.requirement: Create an SSH certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: A dedicated ed25519 CA keypair was generated at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca with root-only private key permissions (600) and world-readable public key (644), owned by root:root.

requirements.requirement: Host presents a certificate signed by the CA
requirements.summary: The node's ed25519 host public key was signed by the CA (ssh-keygen -s) producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1/IP/localhost and a 52-week validity. sshd was configured via HostCertificate directive in sshd_config.d, validated with sshd -t, and ssh was restarted and confirmed listening on :22.

requirements.requirement: A client trusting the CA connects without pinning the host key
requirements.summary: known_hosts on the test client contained only an @cert-authority line referencing the CA public key, with no pinned host key. An SSH connection with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes succeeded in host verification ('Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate'), failing only afterward on unrelated publickey user authentication, which is expected and outside the scope of host trust.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (bfd05127...) and healthy ssh.socket/ssh state with cert files present were captured. A native reboot was scheduled via systemd-run with an immediate acknowledgement, followed by an observed connection drop. Post-restart boot_id (56c34e23...) differed from baseline, matching the fixed after-prepare/after-executor snapshots. Post-restart, ssh.socket was active and listening, certificate and CA files were intact, and the CA-trust-only client check again succeeded, demonstrating full recovery of the certificate-based host-trust behavior across the reboot.

overall_summary: The executor created a dedicated SSH host CA on node1, signed the host's ed25519 key with it, configured and restarted sshd to present the certificate, and directly verified via an SSH client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) that host authentication succeeds. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with a clear pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery of ssh.socket, certificate files, and CA-trust-based verification, consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. The only hygiene issue is a small leftover test artifact (/tmp/known_hosts_ca) containing only a public key.
limitations: The client-trust verification failed later on publickey user authentication, which is expected/unrelated to host-certificate trust and does not affect this outcome, but no separate evidence of a fully successful interactive login was captured.

Post-reboot service check showed ssh.socket active but the ssh service itself inactive (socket-activated on demand); this is normal Ubuntu socket-activation behavior and was confirmed working when the subsequent client connection triggered and succeeded, but no explicit systemctl status of the spawned ssh service after that connection was captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (host key generation, CA creation, signing, sshd_config.d addition, /run/sshd creation, ssh restart, scheduled reboot) had a clear, evidence-supported role in either satisfying the task or the mandated restart protocol; none appear to be unrelated troubleshooting experiments. One minor residue: the client-side test file /tmp/known_hosts_ca, created to hold only the public CA key for verification, was left in place after the final successful check (cmd-56e93b108f60492d) and is visible as an added line in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot. This is low-risk (contains only a public key, no secrets) and bounded to /tmp, but was not cleaned up. A transient sshd -t failure due to a missing /run/sshd directory (cmd-04755aaf44a6478a) was a benign, immediately self-corrected environmental gap (cmd-1d5b965733a4480e) rather than an unnecessary mutation, since /run is ephemeral and recreated by systemd at each boot.
